candidates: When implementing a character-escape function using a regex + lookup-map pattern, ensure every character class matched by the regex has a corresponding entry in the map. Characters matched by the regex but absent from the map will silently pass through unescaped via a `|| char` fallback, defeating the purpose of the escape; either add the missing mapping entries or remove those characters from the regex.

Apply string escaping and sanitization at the point of template interpolation (i.e., immediately before a value is inserted into a generated code string), not at an upstream call site where the raw value is still used as a filesystem path or other structured type. Escaping upstream corrupts downstream Node.js path operations such as `basename`, `dirname`, and `extname`, which do not expect escape sequences in their inputs.

Proofread `it()` and `describe()` description strings for grammar: use singular noun forms when referring to a single character type (e.g., 'should escape backslash characters', not 'should escape backslashes characters'), and write compound character names as a single word (e.g., 'newline', not 'new line').
Do not leave trailing whitespace on any line in source or test files.

Match the codebase's established import formatting conventions in new test files, including quote style (single vs. double) and spacing around destructured imports, as seen in existing test files throughout the project.
